records.statement: In the English version of Karel Čapek's play R. U. R. (1923), the Robots' leader Radius proclaims that the power of man has fallen and that a new world, the rule of the Robots, has arisen; a manifesto read earlier in the play says the Robots are more highly developed than man, stronger and more intelligent.

records.qualification: Fiction: a stage play. The Robots are manufactured workers made from a synthetic living substance; the play calls them machines, and under decision 7a they count as machine intelligence on W01, B6 and U02 alike. Lines spoken by characters document what the play stages, not Čapek's view. The Czech printing of 1920 (Aventinum) carries the counterpart passage (pp. [80] and 57), as read by the cross-family check on page images; the English wording is not dated from it.

records.qualification: Fiction. The control half of B6, staged as an event: the play's people cannot stop the Robots they made. Earlier in the play a manager says the Robots have no will of their own. Butler's letter of 1863 remains B6's earliest located text. The Robots are manufactured from a synthetic living substance; under decision 7a they count as machines (see the W01 record). The evidence is a single line of dialogue whose immediate object is the Robots unloading arms; it is a narrow staged instance, not a general statement about control of machines. The Czech printing of 1920 (Aventinum) carries the counterpart passage (p. 61), as read by the cross-family check on page images; the English wording is not dated from it.

records.qualification: Fiction; characters' lines document what the play stages, not Čapek's view. The Robots are synthetic organisms made from a living substance; the play calls them machines and ascribes them intelligence, and under decision 7a they count as machines on U02 as on W01 and B6. Later in the play Dr Gall says that they have 'ceased to be machines', one character's claim. The Czech printing of 1920 (Aventinum) calls them 'živé a inteligentní pracovní stroje' (p. 12) and carries the counterpart of the intelligence line (p. 13), as read by the cross-family check on page images; the English wording is not dated from it.

crossFamily.result: disagreement, open for the maintainer: the pack records context, the checker articulates.

readings.pack (Claude): context: the Robots are made from a synthetic living substance; the play ascribes intelligence to them but does not state that a machine could think.
readings.checker (Codex): articulates: the play calls the Robots machines (Czech p. 12, “živé a inteligentní pracovní stroje”) and ascribes them intelligence; a mechanism-only boundary for U02 while W01 and B6 are recorded for the same beings needs a stated scope decision.

crossFamily2.result: material, second pass: the checker holds reading a (the Robots count as machines for U02 as for W01 and B6, with the synthetic-organism qualification and speaker attribution); a uniformly non-biological boundary would give c on all three. Settles decision 7 as recommended.

maintainerDecision.effect: Recorded as articulating U02, as fiction, with the synthetic-organism qualification (settled by the second pass agreeing with the recommendation).
